source_validation_really_blocks.claim: 来源校验确实在拦 —— MISSING_FIELD_TRACE 证明防线有效；正因为防线有效，才暴露出提示词缺陷。
evidence: every rejection in this batch is the same stable code, MISSING_FIELD_TRACE, raised by source_validation.py:110 when the traced field set differs from the expected set

the rejection is structural, not cosmetic: the model returned a schema-valid candidate whose promises carried no trace at all, so the validator refused a candidate that the HTTP adapter had already accepted
the validator refused 5 of 5 v1 attempts and 7 of 9 v2 attempts, i.e. it is not a formality that any output passes
because the validator refused instead of guessing, the defect surfaced as a named code with the exact missing fields recorded, which is what made the prompt-side repair possible at all

open_questions_for_the_independent_verif: why the same request body (the run id inside metadata is stripped by the shared shim, so the upstream request is identical) produced an accepted candidate once and the identical rejection otherwise; upstream prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens was 0 on the v1 capture and 5120 on the v2 capture, and whether that prefix cache contributes to the bimodality is not established by this evidence

whether the batch should keep trying the documented command until an accepted run lands in reports/batches/BATCH-28/live, or record the accepted run exactly as produced (this round did the latter: reports/batches/BATCH-28/live holds the rejected run C, and the two accepted runs are preserved beside it)

tools/verification/live_smoke.py in the tree at f76dd1c3 and ab3dba9 calls service._compile_from_server_facts / _enrich_extracted_journey / _aggregate_server_evidence, but those three helpers are module-level functions in covenia_b.services.analyze, not AnalyzeService members (only _validate_candidate is a static method on the service). That revision therefore cannot reach exit 0 at all: an accepted candidate raises AttributeError before the journey is built. RESOLVED during this round: the concurrent session committed the journey-projection fix as 2cb393e, and the committed blob (sha256 dd6213687dd0c48c32a37a2ff4bf29e2081acbf986b9ff04d1eede013e6f64bd) is byte-identical to the file both accepted runs were produced with, so the accepted artifacts are reproducible from HEAD. The verifier should still confirm which revision the acceptance is recorded against.

the model's own output for one and the same request body is bimodal across attempts (3 observations + 1 promise with observation traces only, versus the same plus candidate_promise_texts[0]); no explanation is established here, and a run that is stopped at the first accepted attempt will record only the accepted sample, so any acceptance rate quoted from single runs should be read as a lower bound on the retry cost, not as a property of the prompt
